Stamp Duty Land Tax - Residential property rates. You usually pay Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) on increasing portions of the property price when you buy residential property, for example a house or flat. The amount you pay depends on:. • when you bought the property. • how much you paid for it. • whether you’re eligible for relief or an exemption. Rates for a single property. You pay SDLT at these rates if, after buying the property, it is the only residential property you own. You will usually pay 5% on top of these rates if you own another residential property. Rates from 1 April 2025. Property or lease premium or transfer value SDLT rate. Up to £125,000 Zero. The next £125,000 (the portion from £125,001 to £250,000) 2%. The next £675,000 (the portion from £250,001 to £925,000) 5%. The next £575,000 (the portion from £925,001 to £1.5 million) 10%. The remaining amount (the portion above £1.5 million) 12%. Example. In April 2025 you buy a house for £295,000. The SDLT you owe will be calculated as follows:. • 0% on the first £125,000 = £0. • 2% on the second £125,000 = £2,500. • 5% on the final £45,000 = £2,250. • total SDLT = £4,750. 4 BEDROOM EXTENDED DETACHED FAMILY HOME. Situated in a popular and established residential location in Erdington, this attractive dormer bungalow offers particularly versatile accommodation, making it an excellent purchase for a variety of buyers. The property occupies a particularly desirable position along a private, unadopted and tree-lined road, offering a peaceful setting with a distinctly rural feel, almost reminiscent of a country lane. With no through traffic or pedestrian access for non-residents, the road enjoys an exceptionally quiet and secluded atmosphere, making it one of the most peaceful locations in the Erdington area. The private road arrangement is an important feature for prospective purchasers to be aware of. The property is approached via a paved front garden with a gated entrance and benefits from an area of off-road parking situated opposite the front entrance, which forms part of the property's ownership. Internally, the accommodation begins with a welcoming entrance hallway providing access to the ground-floor rooms. The front lounge is a good-sized reception room featuring a decorative fireplace, while there are two ground-floor bedrooms, including a rear bedroom with wood-effect flooring and an adjoining snug area. The snug provides useful additional living space and features patio doors opening directly onto the rear garden, together with an attractive glass feature window separating it from the bedroom. The ground floor also includes a fully tiled wet room bathroom, fitted with a shower, wash basin and WC. The fitted kitchen offers a good range of wall and base units, a central island incorporating the sink, a double oven, four-ring gas hob and extractor hood, together with space for additional appliances. A separate utility room provides further practical space and leads to a useful downstairs WC, which also houses the gas combination boiler. From the kitchen, a staircase leads to the first floor where the third bedroom is located. This is a well-proportioned room with a rear-facing double-glazed window and useful eaves storage. Externally, the rear garden has been designed for ease of maintenance, with paved and manageable areas, enclosed boundaries and useful side access. There is also a substantial purpose-built outbuilding at the bottom of the garden, providing excellent additional storage space. The property is conveniently positioned for a range of local shops, supermarkets and everyday amenities, with further shopping and leisure facilities available in Erdington and Sutton Coldfield town centres. There are schools for children of various ages within the surrounding area, together with nearby public transport services and Erdington railway station, providing connections towards Birmingham and beyond. The property is also well placed for access to the A38, providing convenient road links into Birmingham city centre and the wider motorway network. A spacious and versatile dormer bungalow offering a great deal of accommodation, useful outside space and the considerable attraction of an exceptionally peaceful, tree-lined private road setting, all within a convenient Erdington location. Inspired by the vision of HM King Charles III and evolved by the Duchy of Cornwall over more than two decades, Nansledan features charismatic streetscapes and sustainable urban design. Led by an award-winning site manager praised for exceptional craftsmanship, our homes embody character and quality, and are future-proofed with the inclusion of air source heat pumps, solar PV panels, and electric car charging points. text: Situated within the highly regarded sought-after coastal village of Mullion, this spacious, well presented three bedroom home is being offered for sale chain-free. Offering generous and versatile accommodation, this property is ideally suited for family living or those seeking a property in a desirable part of Cornwall. The property also presents an excellent opportunity for buyers looking for a potentially straight-forward purchase. The accommodation comprises of a sitting room, dining area, separate kitchen, conservatory and a garage on the ground floor along with three bedrooms and a bathroom on the first floor. A particularly useful addition is the conservatory, creating an additional reception space and an ideal spot to relax and enjoy the garden throughout the seasons. To the outside, the property benefits from both front and rear gardens. The sizeable front garden is predominantly laid to lawn, providing an attractive approach to the property, whilst the enclosed rear garden offers a pleasant outdoor space for relaxing, gardening or entertaining. A garage and driveway provide convenient off-road parking and additional storage. Combining spacious accommodation, attractive gardens, a garage and driveway parking with an enviable village location close to the Cornish coastline, this property offers an excellent opportunity to enjoy a relaxed lifestyle in one of Cornwall's most desirable locations. An early viewing is strongly recommended. Colroger Close is situated within the popular and well established village of Mullion - one of the largest and most sought-after villages on the beautiful Lizard Peninsula in South Cornwall. Offering a wonderful balance of village convenience, community atmosphere and access to the spectacular Cornish coastline, Mullion is an excellent location for those looking to enjoy a relaxed coastal lifestyle. The village itself offers a good range of everyday amenities, including local shops, convenience stores, cafés, traditional Public Houses, restaurants and independent businesses. There are also primary and secondary schooling facilities, a health centre and pharmacy together with a variety of community groups and recreational activities. A particular attraction of the area is its beautiful surrounding coastline, with miles of scenic coastal walks and an abundance of picturesque beaches and secluded coves close by. Mullion Cove is a charming historic harbour, cared for by the National Trust, nestled beneath rugged cliffs and offering wonderful coastal scenery. Nearby Polurrian Cove and Poldhu Cove are particularly popular, with sandy beaches, opportunities for surfing, swimming and coastal walks along the renowned South West Coast Path. For a wider range of retail, leisure and commercial facilities, the nearby market town of Helston is approximately five miles distant, offering supermarkets, high street retailers, restaurants, leisure facilities and further schooling options. The location also provides a convenient base for exploring the wider Lizard Peninsula, including its picturesque villages, unspoilt countryside and renowned beauty spots. Combining excellent village amenities with easy access to some of Cornwall's finest beaches and coastal scenery, Mullion remains a particularly desirable location for families, retirees and those looking to embrace the very best of coastal living. SITUATION AND DESCRIPTION Occupying a truly exceptional waterfront position in the heart of the highly sought-after village of Bere Ferrers, this fascinating three-bedroom period home enjoys superb, uninterrupted views across the River Tavy towards the far banks. Rich in character and local history, the property combines wonderfully generous accommodation with a setting that is difficult to rival. Believed to date back more than 200 years in part, the property was originally three separate cottages, with the three original entrances still identifiable on an old photograph of the property – two positioned to the front and a third to the side, accessed from the road. For many years it played an important role within village life as the local shop and Post Office, before subsequently being converted to create the spacious and comfortable single home seen today. Its history remains very much part of its charm, with exposed beams, stonework, fireplaces and other period details found throughout. The accommodation is particularly generous, extending to approximately 1,791 sq ft, with three substantial reception rooms providing a great deal of versatility. The main sitting room is an impressive space, measuring approximately 19'7" x 14'4", with a characterful exposed stone wall and fireplace housing a wood-burning stove creating an attractive focal point. The fireplace also retains its original Cloam oven, a particularly interesting reminder of the property's age and history. From here, the property's wonderful position beside the river can be fully appreciated, with the outlook across the water providing an ever-changing backdrop. The dining room is another excellent-sized reception space and continues the character of the house, again benefiting from a wood-burning stove and exposed overhead beams. A further living room provides a third generous reception room, making the ground floor exceptionally flexible for entertaining, family life or those requiring a separate study or snug. The kitchen is positioned alongside the dining room and is fitted with a range of units and work surfaces. Completing the ground-floor accommodation is a useful shower room. Upstairs, the generous proportions continue with three well-sized bedrooms. The two principal bedrooms are particularly spacious, while the third is also a comfortable double room. Several rooms enjoy the property's remarkable outlook, taking full advantage of its position overlooking the river and surrounding landscape. A family bathroom completes the first-floor accommodation. Outside, immediately to the rear of the property is a small enclosed courtyard, providing a private and easily accessible space for outdoor dining, relaxing or enjoying a morning coffee. A small garden shed is positioned at the rear of the courtyard, providing useful additional storage. In addition, the property benefits from a separate parcel of garden situated just a few yards from the front door beside the reedbeds. This provides a further outdoor space in which to sit and enjoy the surroundings. The location is undoubtedly one of the home's defining features. For those looking for something genuinely individual, this is a rare opportunity to acquire a historic village home of considerable character and proportions, positioned right on the waterfront with spectacular views across the River Tavy. Bere Ferrers is an attractive waterside village situated on the Bere Peninsula between the Rivers Tavy and Tamar, surrounded by beautiful countryside and estuary scenery. The village has a strong sense of community and is a small village with a charming, old-fashioned pub which serves homemade food, railway station, café/shop and historic riverside church. There is a social club and a Saturday Market in the village hall where one can buy local produce. The unspoilt surroundings of the Tamar Valley with its rolling hills, meandering rivers and ancient woodlands are ideally suited to those who enjoy walking, riding and water sports and is ideal for sailing enthusiasts with a nearby sailing club and moorings. There are countryside walks and beautiful landscapes to admire within moments of leaving the door, including Dartmoor National Park, which is around 20 minutes by road. Perfect for those who enjoy being away from the bustle of modern life without being disconnected, Bere Ferrers benefits from its own railway station on the picturesque Tamar Valley Line. Bere Ferrers railway station is sited at the top of the village and goes directly into Plymouth within 20 minutes, then onto Exeter and in turn into London Paddington, which can be reached in around 4 hours. Situated 1.5 miles away is the village of Bere Alston which has a wide range of shopping facilities as well as a post office, doctors’ surgery, chemist, and a highly rated primary school. The village is situated approximately 6 miles from Tavistock and about 10 miles from Plymouth. There is a regular train service to and from Plymouth and a regular bus service to and from Tavistock. text: £900,000 - £950,000. Hampstead Road, Brighton | Substantial Five-Bedroom Victorian Family Home with Versatile Living Space and Landscaped Garden. An impressive and beautifully presented five-bedroom Victorian family home, offering spacious and versatile accommodation arranged over three floors. Situated on the desirable Hampstead Road in Brighton, this characterful property combines elegant period features with contemporary interiors, generous living spaces and a beautifully arranged rear garden. The street also benefits from convenient permit and paid parking options, with greater parking availability than many neighbouring roads, thanks to residential properties occupying just one side of the street. The property immediately impresses with its attractive period façade and welcoming entrance hallway, featuring original patterned floor tiles, decorative detailing and a staircase that sets the tone for the character found throughout. The ground floor offers two generous reception rooms, providing excellent flexibility for modern family living. The principal living room is a particularly impressive space, with a large bay window enjoying elevated views across Brighton, an attractive feature fireplace, bespoke shelving and ample room for both relaxing and dining. A second reception room provides an inviting additional living area, complete with a decorative fireplace, fitted shelving and French doors opening onto the courtyard, making it ideal as a family room, snug or entertaining space. To the rear, the spacious contemporary kitchen and dining room forms the heart of the home. Beautifully designed with sleek white cabinetry, contrasting worktops, a central island with breakfast bar seating and generous dining space, it offers the perfect setting for everyday family life and entertaining. Large sliding doors connect the kitchen to the courtyard, creating a wonderful flow between indoor and outdoor living and the ground floor cloakroom provides additional practicality. The first floor offers three well-proportioned bedrooms, each with its own individual character. The impressive bay-fronted principal bedroom on this floor enjoys elevated views, original wooden flooring and a beautiful period fireplace. An office (or additional bedroom) and a stylish family bathroom completes this floor. The second floor provides two further bedrooms and an additional bathroom, creating an excellent arrangement for growing families, guests or older children seeking their own space. The beautifully finished bathroom features a freestanding roll-top bath, separate shower, patterned flooring and elegant brass fittings. Throughout the property, a thoughtful combination of period charm and contemporary styling creates a home full of personality, with original fireplaces, decorative cornicing, large sash windows and carefully considered interiors. Outside, the property benefits from a delightful rear garden arranged across different levels, incorporating decked seating areas, established planting and space for outdoor dining and entertaining. The garden provides a wonderful retreat from city life, while the courtyard immediately adjoining the kitchen offers an additional outdoor seating area. Hampstead Road is a highly desirable residential address in Brighton, conveniently positioned for the independent shops, cafés and restaurants of Seven Dials, as well as Brighton Station and Preston Park Station (approx. 2 min walk), excellent local schools and the city centre. The nearby green spaces of Preston Park provide further appeal for families and those seeking an active outdoor lifestyle. Combining generous proportions, period elegance, contemporary living and a sought-after Brighton location, this exceptional family home offers a wonderful opportunity to enjoy the very best of city living.

A beautifully presented and wonderfully characterful Grade II listed two-bedroom home, enviably positioned at the top of Victoria Street within the highly sought-after Montpelier & Clifton Hill Conservation Area. Full of charm, warmth and individuality, this much-loved home has been exceptionally well cared for by the current owners and offers a rare combination of period character, beautifully maintained interiors and exceptional outside space. The accommodation is arranged over two floors and retains a wealth of charming period features, including elegant bow windows, original fireplaces, timber flooring and beautifully detailed interiors, while having been thoughtfully maintained to create a comfortable and inviting home. The impressive through lounge/dining room provides a wonderful heart to the home, with elegant proportions, a feature fireplace and bow window to the front, flowing through to the dining area at the rear and providing direct access to the garden. The well-appointed kitchen is positioned to the rear and is both practical and beautifully presented, with a good range of storage and worktop space. At the far end, a charming breakfast seating area creates an additional informal space for dining or relaxing, with views towards the garden. Upstairs are two well-proportioned bedrooms, with the principal bedroom enjoying the elevated outlook and sea views, alongside a stylish shower room. One of the property's most exceptional features is its outside space. The secluded patio garden is beautifully established and wonderfully private, providing a peaceful setting for outdoor dining and entertaining. Beyond this, and an extremely rare feature for a home of this type, is a separate roof terrace offering further space to sit and enjoy the elevated position and sea views. To have both a garden and a roof terrace in this location is a particularly unusual and desirable combination!. The property is situated in one of Brighton's most sought-after residential areas, within the Montpelier & Clifton Hill Conservation Area and close to the wealth of independent shops, cafés, restaurants and amenities of Seven Dials, Western Road and central Brighton. The seafront is also within easy reach, while Brighton Station is conveniently accessible for commuters. Offered for sale with no onward chain, this is a truly charming period home that combines character, excellent presentation and an exceptional selection of outside spaces in a highly desirable elevated location. The Kitchen is the heart of this home with ample worksurface and a range cooker, the large dining table is excellent for entertaining, while the sitting area adjoined is perfect to sit in and appreciate the view. The Family room is the cosiest room in the house with log burner on, perfect for enjoying some television. The sunroom connects the property with outside especially in the warmer weather. The principal room is located off the hall from the formal lounge, it enjoys a 27m² footprint, dual aspect allowing natural light in abundance, walk in closet and ensuite bathroom. The second bedroom is at the rear of the property with its own large dressing area, separate bathroom and dual aspect windows. Both upstairs bedrooms are doubles sharing a bathroom. The ground floor also benefits room a large storage room, W.C, utility and storage barn which also grants access to the car port. Garden. The property is set within a generous garden which extends to approximately 2 acres and is mostly laid to lawn enclosed by some shrubs and trees to the south and west. There is a large gravel driveway to the east of the property which provides ample space for parking vehicles. Buildings. The buildings at Braeface Farmhouse comprise:. Log store (9.50m x 8.30m). Of traditional stone construction under a pitched slate roof with a concrete floor. There is a small lean-to extension to the front of the building of timber and steel construction under a felt roof. Bothy (3.80m x 3.00m). Of stone construction under a pitched slate roof with a concrete floor. Additionally, there are equestrian facilities which are situated just to the north of the farmhouse, briefly they comprise:. Timber Stable Block (21.50m x 4.85m) + (7.33m x 4.85m). Of timber frame construction under a corrugated felt roof and a concrete floor. Accommodating 6 stables, tack room and feed stores. There is a turnout pen situated adjacent to the stable block. Outdoor Riding Arena. Adjacent to the stable block there is a riding arena with a sand surface enclosed with post and rail fencing. The Land. The land at Braeface Farmhouse extends to 4.84 Ha (11.96 Acres) and is split into two paddocks which are currently down to pasture and utilised for grazing livestock. The land is situated to the south of the farmhouse and is accessed via the main access road and a farm track. The land is predominately east facing and has been classified as being Grade 4.1 and 4.2 by the James Hutton Institute. The fields benefit from private source water supply. Method of sale. Situated in the charming Oxfordshire hamlet of Taston, Lutleys and Blacksmiths Cottage represent a truly unique offering. For the first time in over half a century, these neighbouring period cottages are available together, presenting a remarkable opportunity to create an exceptional country home in a peaceful and highly sought-after setting. Believed to have been designed by the noted Victorian architect J.P. Seddon and formerly part of the Ditchley Estate, the cottages are steeped in local history and are even referenced in Pevsner's Guide to Oxfordshire. Surrounded by unspoilt countryside, they occupy a generous plot with mature gardens and a paddock and enjoy a wonderful sense of privacy and tranquillity. Lutleys benefits from a beautifully proportioned south-facing garden, while Blacksmiths enjoys attractive views across open farmland with woodland beyond. Both properties offer ample parking and extensive outdoor space, creating an enviable setting for family life or a countryside retreat. Planning permission has been granted for the sympathetic extension of both cottages, allowing buyers the opportunity to enhance and modernise the accommodation while preserving the character of the original buildings. Furthermore, ownership of both properties presents the exciting prospect of creating a single substantial residence, subject to the necessary consents. Combining architectural heritage, generous grounds and significant potential, this is an exceptionally rare opportunity to acquire two characterful period cottages in a peaceful and unspoilt rural setting. Rich in history yet offering considerable scope for enhancement, the properties provide an unusual chance from which to create a truly special country home. With mature gardens, far-reaching views across surrounding countryside and planning consent already in place, the combination of lifestyle, heritage and opportunity is particularly compelling. Set within one of Oxfordshire's most picturesque hamlets, opportunities of this nature are seldom available and are unlikely to be repeated for many years to come. Taston is a picturesque and peaceful hamlet surrounded by rolling Oxfordshire countryside, approximately four miles south of Chipping Norton. Offering a quintessential rural setting, it enjoys easy access to the town's excellent amenities, independent shops, restaurants and schooling, as well as the wider attractions of the Cotswolds. A spacious three-storey townhouse offering flexible family living in one of Suffolk’s most well-connected villages. Beautifully presented throughout, this impressive home combines generous accommodation with modern practicality, featuring three double bedrooms, including a superb principal suite occupying the entire top floor. Offering space, versatility and convenience in equal measure, this is a home perfectly suited to modern family life. The Location Red Lodge is a popular and well-connected Suffolk village, ideally positioned between Mildenhall and Newmarket, with excellent access to both the A11 and A14, making it a convenient base for commuters travelling towards Cambridge, Bury St Edmunds, Ipswich and beyond. The nearby railway station at Kennet, approximately two miles away, provides additional transport links, while regular bus services connect the village with surrounding towns and villages. Once a small rural settlement, Red Lodge has grown into a thriving and highly regarded community, offering an excellent balance of countryside living and modern convenience. The village takes its name from the historic Red Lodge Inn, a building dating back to the 17th Century and believed to have once served as a hunting lodge. Today, it remains a popular local venue, known for its restaurant and welcoming atmosphere. For those who enjoy the outdoors, Red Lodge Heath is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest, renowned for its unique landscape and important wildlife habitats. The surrounding Suffolk countryside offers a wealth of walking, cycling and recreational opportunities, whilst nearby Newmarket provides access to the internationally renowned home of British horse racing, complete with racecourses, museums and year-round events. The village itself benefits from a wide range of amenities that continue to grow alongside the community. These include a Primary School, an Ecumenical church, village hall and the well-used Millennium Centre, which hosts various clubs, activities and community events throughout the year. Recreational facilities include tennis courts, sports pitches, a pavilion and allotments, helping to foster a strong sense of community. A modern village centre, opened in 2014, provides convenient day-to-day amenities including a convenience store, pharmacy, takeaway outlets, hair salon and other local services. Residents also benefit from easy access to larger shopping, leisure and healthcare facilities in both Mildenhall and Newmarket. Red Lodge is particularly well regarded for its leisure attractions. Red Lodge Karting is recognised as one of the country's largest karting venues, while nearby Wildtracks Outdoor Activity Park offers a variety of pursuits including archery, motocross, off-roading and other outdoor activities. Together with nearby golf courses, equestrian facilities and nature reserves, the area offers something to suit a wide range of interests and lifestyles. The wider coastline provides an array of scenic walks and beaches, while the nearby Georgian town of Holt offers further shopping, dining and schooling options. The village itself benefits from a strong community feel, with three churches in the wider setting and popular local pubs including the The Wiveton Bell and The Three Swallows both within walking distance. The house is beautifully presented and provides well-proportioned accommodation arranged over two floors. The spacious reception hall leads to a cloakroom, dining room/snug with French doors opening onto the garden, and a well-equipped kitchen/breakfast room with a generous utility room beyond. The sitting room is positioned at the rear of the house and features a stone fireplace with a log/solid fuel burner and French doors opening directly onto the garden, making the most of the attractive rural outlook. A large ground floor bedroom with en suite bathroom provides a particularly useful additional dimension to the accommodation and could suit a variety of requirements, including guest accommodation, a home office or an additional reception room. There is extensive parking together with a detached double garage, while the beautifully maintained gardens extend around three sides of the house and include mature planting and several discreet seating areas. The rear garden is especially attractive, overlooking open fields and countryside beyond. Freehold. Oxenton is a small and attractive rural hamlet situated in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty at the foot of Oxenton Hill, on the edge of the Cotswolds.
